# Honestkit

> Small, honest developer tools: privacy-friendly browser extensions, free in-browser tools, Apify data tools, and Python error guides where every code block was run and its output pasted unedited. AI-assisted, open source, no tracking.

## Browser extensions
- [PlainHeaders](https://honestkit.github.io/plainheaders/): Add, change or remove HTTP request & response headers. Open source, no tracking, access only to sites you choose.
- [PlainTables](https://honestkit.github.io/plaintables/): Copy any web table to Excel, Google Sheets, CSV or Markdown in one click. No row limits, no account, no tracking.
- [MDGrab](https://honestkit.github.io/mdgrab/): Turn any article or selection into clean Markdown for Obsidian, notes or LLM prompts. No signup, no limits, no tracking.
- [PlainLinks](https://honestkit.github.io/plainlinks/): Extract every link on a page or selection: dedupe, filter by text or regex, copy or export to CSV/XLSX. No tracking.
- [PlainInspect](https://honestkit.github.io/plaininspect/): Hover any text to see its font, size, weight and colors. See every font and color a page uses. No tracking.

## Free in-browser tools
- [DNS lookup + SPF, DMARC & MX checker](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/dns-lookup/): Look up a domain's A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA and SOA records and check its email setup: MX present, one valid SPF record, DMARC policy. Paste a domain, URL or email address.
- [HTML table to CSV / TSV / Markdown](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/html-table-to-csv/): Paste HTML and convert every table to CSV, TSV (for Excel / Google Sheets), Markdown or XLSX. Handles colspan and rowspan. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Markdown table to Excel / CSV](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/markdown-table-to-excel/): Paste a Markdown table (or a whole README) and get CSV, TSV to paste into Excel or Google Sheets, or a real .xlsx file. Strips **bold**, `code` and link syntax, unescapes \|. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Excel / CSV to JSON converter](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/excel-to-json/): Paste cells from Excel or Google Sheets (or CSV) and get a JSON array of objects, with numbers and TRUE/FALSE typed, empty cells as null, and optional nesting of address.city-style headers. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [robots.txt tester](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/robots-txt-tester/): Paste a robots.txt and a list of URLs: see which are allowed or blocked for any user agent, and which rule decides, using Google's matching rules (longest match, Allow wins ties, * and $). Runs in your browser.
- [hreflang checker](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/hreflang-checker/): Paste a page's HTML (or its hreflang link tags, or sitemap xhtml:link entries) and check every hreflang: valid language and country codes, absolute URLs, x-default, self-reference and duplicates. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [CSV to SQL INSERT converter](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/csv-to-sql/): Paste CSV or cells from Excel and get a CREATE TABLE plus batched INSERT statements with inferred column types, NULLs for empty cells and correct quoting per database. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [XML to CSV / Excel converter](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/xml-to-csv/): Paste XML (an export, RSS feed, sitemap or API response) and get one row per repeating element as CSV, TSV, Markdown or .xlsx. Attributes, nested and repeated elements become columns. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Compare two lists](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/compare-two-lists/): Paste two lists (emails, SKUs, names, URLs, a column from Excel) and see what is only in the first, only in the second, and in both. Ignores case and spaces if you want. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [JWT decoder (local)](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/jwt-decoder/): Decode a JSON Web Token's header and payload in your browser, with iat / nbf / exp shown as UTC dates and an expiry check. The token never leaves the page: no server, no analytics. Accepts a pasted Authorization: Bearer header.
- [Transpose CSV](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/transpose-csv/): Swap the rows and columns of a CSV or TSV: the first column becomes the header row. Quoted fields with commas or line breaks are kept intact and short rows are padded. Copy, or download CSV / .xlsx. Runs in your browser.
- [Split CSV file](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/split-csv-file/): Split a large CSV into smaller files: every N rows, or one file per value of a column (e.g. one per region). Each part keeps the header row; download all parts as one .zip. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Merge CSV files](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/merge-csv-files/): Combine several CSV files into one: columns are matched by header name even when the order differs, missing columns stay empty, and a source_file column records where each row came from. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [CSP & security headers generator](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/security-headers/): Build a strict Content-Security-Policy plus HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and nosniff, and export as raw headers, nginx, Apache, Netlify/Cloudflare _headers, Express or a meta tag.
- [curl to fetch / Python / axios](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/curl-converter/): Paste a curl command (e.g. from DevTools “Copy as cURL”) and get equivalent JavaScript fetch(), Python requests or Node axios code. Headers, JSON and form bodies, -G query data, multipart -F uploads, basic auth and cookies handled.
- [JSON to Markdown table](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/json-to-markdown-table/): Paste a JSON array or API response and get a GitHub-flavored Markdown table. Nested objects become dot-notation columns; missing keys are left blank. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [JSON to CSV / Excel](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/json-to-csv/): Paste a JSON array (or an API response) and convert it to CSV, TSV, Markdown or XLSX. Nested objects become dot-notation columns. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Excel / Google Sheets to Markdown table](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/excel-to-markdown-table/): Copy cells in Excel or Google Sheets, paste them here and get a GitHub-flavored Markdown table (or HTML table). Pipes and line breaks in cells are handled. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Markdown table formatter](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/markdown-table-formatter/): Paste a messy Markdown table (or a whole Markdown file) and get evenly padded, aligned columns. Keeps :--- / :---: / ---: alignment, escaped pipes and inline code. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [CSV to Markdown table](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/csv-to-markdown-table/): Paste CSV, TSV or semicolon-separated data and get a GitHub-flavored Markdown table or a clean HTML table. Quotes, commas and line breaks inside cells are handled. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [HTML to Markdown converter](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/html-to-markdown/): Convert HTML to clean Markdown: headings, paragraphs, links, lists, code blocks, bold/italic and GitHub-flavoured tables. Runs locally in your browser.
- [Markdown to HTML converter](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/markdown-to-html/): Convert Markdown to clean HTML: headings, lists (nested), links, images, code blocks, blockquotes, GitHub tables and strikethrough. Raw HTML is escaped by default. Runs in your browser.
- [Extract links from HTML](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/extract-links/): Paste HTML and extract every link with its anchor text, rel and target. Dedupe, filter by text or regex, resolve relative URLs and export CSV. Runs in your browser.
- [UTM link builder (single & bulk)](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/utm-builder/): Add utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term and utm_content to one link or a whole list. Keeps existing query parameters and #fragments, replaces old UTM values, exports CSV. Runs in your browser.
- [URL parser, encoder & decoder](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/url-parser/): Paste a URL to see protocol, user, host (punycode and Unicode), port, path, every query parameter (duplicates kept) and the #fragment. Percent-encode or decode text three ways, with clear errors for bad escapes.
- [Sitemap.xml generator from URL list](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/sitemap-generator/): Paste a list of URLs and get a valid sitemap.xml: duplicates removed, invalid and relative URLs flagged, special characters XML-escaped, optional lastmod, changefreq and priority, auto-split over 50,000 URLs.
- [HTTP header parser & converter](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/http-headers/): Paste raw HTTP request headers (or a curl command, or JSON) and convert them to a JSON object, curl -H flags, a fetch() headers object or a Python requests dict.
- [Color contrast checker (WCAG)](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/color-contrast-checker/): Check the WCAG 2.x contrast ratio of a text and background color, see AA / AAA pass or fail for normal text, large text and UI components, and get the nearest passing color. Hex, rgb() and hsl().
- [Color palette to CSS variables / Tailwind](https://honestkit.github.io/tools/color-palette-to-css/): Paste a list of hex colors (optionally named) and get CSS custom properties, SCSS variables, a Tailwind v4 @theme block, a Tailwind v3 config or JSON tokens.

## Data tools on Apify
- [SEO Audit Crawler & Broken Link Checker – Website Health](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/website-seo-audit/): Crawl any website and audit every page: titles, meta descriptions, H1s, canonicals, noindex, broken links, duplicates, Open Graph. $5 per 1,000 pages.
- [DNS Lookup & WHOIS Domain Checker — SPF/DMARC, SSL Expiry](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/domain-whois-dns-ssl/): Check domains in bulk: registrar, creation & expiry dates via RDAP, DNS records, SPF/DMARC and SSL certificate expiry. $2 per 1,000 domains.
- [Sitemap Extractor & Bulk URL Status Checker](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/sitemap-url-status-checker/): Extract every URL from a site's sitemaps and find broken links (404/5xx), redirect chains and noindex pages in bulk. $1 per 1,000 URLs.
- [Website Technology Detector – Tech Stack, CMS & Analytics](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/website-tech-stack-detector/): Detect the CMS, ecommerce platform, frameworks, hosting, analytics pixels, chat and payment tools of any website list, plus email provider. $2 per 1,000.
- [PDF Extractor & Parser – Bulk PDF to Text with Metadata](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/pdf-to-text-extractor/): Extract clean text from PDF URLs in bulk: full text or per page, plus title, author, dates and page count. Flat $0.003 per PDF, LLM/RAG-ready.
- [App Store Reviews Scraper – Apple iOS, Multi-Country](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/apple-app-store-reviews/): Scrape Apple App Store reviews for any app from 40+ countries in one run: rating, text, version, date, votes, plus app rating summary. $0.10 per 1,000 reviews.
- [Job Postings & Career Page Scraper – Workday, Greenhouse, Lever](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/ats-company-jobs/): All open jobs from company career sites on Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Recruitee & Workable in one schema, with salary & descriptions. $1 per 1,000 jobs.
- [Company Enrichment from Domain (Logo, Socials, Tech)](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/company-website-enrichment/): Enrich company domains with name, description, logo, LinkedIn/X/Facebook pages, address, tech stack, email provider and domain age. $2 per 1,000 companies.
- [Email Validator & MX Record Checker – Bulk, Disposable, Role](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/email-syntax-mx-checker/): Validate email lists in bulk: syntax, MX records, disposable and role addresses, typo suggestions. No SMTP probing. $1 per 1,000 emails.
- [Website Screenshot API – Bulk Full Page PNG, JPEG & PDF](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/website-screenshot/): Screenshot many URLs at once: full-page or viewport PNG/JPEG/PDF, desktop or mobile, cookie banners hidden. Public image links in the dataset. $3 per 1,000 screenshots.
- [Bulk PageSpeed Insights, Lighthouse & Core Web Vitals](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/pagespeed-core-web-vitals/): Test many URLs with Lighthouse on mobile and desktop: performance score, LCP, CLS, TBT, fix opportunities. No setup; optional API key adds CrUX field data. $0.02 per test.
- [Article Scraper & Text Extractor – Clean Markdown for LLM/RAG](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/article-extractor/): Extract clean article text, title, author, date and Markdown from any list of URLs. No browser, fast, per-URL errors. $1 per 1,000 articles.
- [Bluesky Posts Scraper – Profiles & Threads, No Login](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/bluesky-posts/): Export Bluesky posts from any profiles and full reply threads with likes, reposts and quotes via the official public API. No login. $0.50 per 1,000 posts.
- [Steam Reviews Scraper – Game Reviews & App Details](https://honestkit.github.io/apify/steam-reviews/): Export Steam game reviews in bulk with playtime, votes, language and recommendation, plus game details and review summary. No login. $0.50 per 1,000 reviews.

## Guides
- [How to check every URL in a sitemap for errors](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/check-all-urls-in-sitemap/): Find broken (404), redirected and erroring URLs in your sitemap.xml with a short shell loop, what to fix for each status code, and how to check large or nested sitemaps.
- [How to check a domain's age and expiry date (free WHOIS / RDAP API)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/domain-age-checker-rdap/): Find when a domain was registered, when it expires and who the registrar is, for free with RDAP, the JSON successor of WHOIS: curl and Python examples, bulk lookups, and the TLDs that publish no dates.
- [How to take a full-page screenshot of a website](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/full-page-screenshot/): Capture an entire scrolling web page as one image: Chrome and Edge DevTools' built-in full-size screenshot, Firefox's Save full page, a one-line Playwright command, and bulk screenshots of many URLs.
- [How to extract text from PDFs (command line, Python and API)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pdf-to-text-api/): Turn PDFs into plain text for search, analysis or LLM pipelines: pdftotext on the command line, pypdf in Python, page ranges and layout mode, reading metadata, and why scanned PDFs return nothing without OCR.
- [How to find broken links on a website (free)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/find-broken-links-on-website/): Check a whole website for broken links for free: a one-line wget spider, a tested Python script that also shows which page links to each broken URL, and how to handle 404s, redirects and false alarms.
- [How to find all pages on a website](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/find-all-pages-on-a-website/): List every page of a website for free: read its sitemap.xml, crawl its links with wget, and compare the two lists to find pages missing from the sitemap and orphan pages. Why one method alone misses pages, with a tested example.
- [How to check if a page is noindex (meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, robots.txt)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/check-noindex/): Find out why a page is not indexed: check the meta robots tag, the X-Robots-Tag header and robots.txt with two tested scripts, plus the robots.txt + noindex trap and a Python robotparser pitfall that reports every URL as blocked.
- [How to check the meta tags of any website](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/check-meta-tags-of-website/): See a page's title, meta description, canonical, robots, Open Graph and Twitter card tags in seconds: a tested browser-console snippet, a curl check of what social previews see, and what to fix.
- [How to check Core Web Vitals (one page or many)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/core-web-vitals-check/): Check Core Web Vitals for free: what PageSpeed Insights shows, lab vs real-user data, the passing thresholds, and a tested Lighthouse script that writes LCP, CLS and blocking time for a list of URLs to CSV.
- [How to convert an HTML table to CSV in Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/html-table-to-csv-python/): A dependency-free Python script that downloads a page, finds every table and writes the one you pick as CSV, with the output from a real Wikipedia table, its limits, and no-code alternatives.
- [How to check a website's HTTP status code](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/check-website-status-code/): Get the HTTP status code of a URL with one curl command, check a whole list into a spreadsheet-ready TSV, and read what 000, 3xx, 4xx and 5xx mean.
- [How to convert JSON to CSV in Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-to-csv-python/): A standard-library Python script that turns a JSON array (or an API response) into CSV, flattens nested objects into address.city-style columns, and handles missing keys, with real output and its limits.
- [How to export App Store reviews to CSV](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/export-app-store-reviews/): Download up to 500 recent reviews per country for any iPhone app into a CSV file with a dependency-free Python script, including the retry Apple's review feed needs, tested on a real app.
- [How to convert CSV to JSON in Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-to-json-python/): A standard-library Python script that converts CSV to a JSON array of objects, auto-detects comma/semicolon/tab, types numbers and true/false, keeps ids with leading zeros as text and rebuilds nested objects from address.city headers.
- [How to convert HTML to Markdown in Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/convert-html-to-markdown-python/): Which Python library converts HTML to Markdown best? markdownify and html2text compared on MDN and Wikipedia pages (code blocks, tables, links), plus a ready script that keeps only the article and fixes relative links.
- [How to block AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, …) with robots.txt](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/block-ai-crawlers-robots-txt/): Copy-paste robots.txt rules that block AI training and AI search crawlers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google-Extended, Apple, Common Crawl, Perplexity, ByteDance, Meta, Amazon) while Google and Bing keep crawling, verified with two parsers.
- [How to convert XML to CSV in Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/xml-to-csv-python/): A standard-library Python script that turns repeating XML elements (RSS items, sitemap URLs, export records) into CSV rows, with attributes, nested and repeated elements as columns and namespaces handled. Tested on real feeds.
- [How to import a CSV into SQLite with Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-to-sqlite-python/): Load a CSV file into an SQLite table with Python's built-in sqlite3 and csv modules: column types inferred from the data, empty cells as NULL, leading-zero ids kept as text, parameterized inserts. Tested on real data.
- [How to split a CSV into multiple files in Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/split-csv-into-multiple-files-python/): A standard-library Python script that splits a CSV every N rows or into one file per value of a column, keeps the header in every part, never cuts a quoted line break, and makes safe file names.
- [How to merge CSV files in Python](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/merge-csv-files-python/): A standard-library Python script that merges many CSV files into one, matches columns by header name even when the order or case differs, keeps columns only some files have, and adds a source_file column.
- [How to compare two lists in Excel](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/compare-two-lists-in-excel/): Two COUNTIF formulas that mark which items of one Excel list are missing from another and which appear in both, how to filter or highlight them, the case-insensitivity catch, and a no-formula alternative.
- [How to remove duplicate lines (Linux, bash, Python)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/remove-duplicate-lines/): Remove duplicate lines from a text file on Linux or macOS: sort -u, the order-preserving awk one-liner, case- and space-insensitive dedupe, counting and listing duplicates with uniq, and a Python one-liner, with real outputs.
- [Content-Security-Policy header examples (nginx, Apache, HTML)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/content-security-policy-header-example/): A working Content-Security-Policy example for nginx, Apache and an HTML meta tag, verified on real servers, plus how to check it with curl and roll it out in report-only mode first.
- [How to check a redirect chain](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/check-redirect-chain/): See every hop of a redirect chain with one curl command, check a list of URLs for hops and final destination, avoid the HEAD-request pitfall, and fix chains so each old URL redirects in one step.
- [How to get a company name from a domain](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/domain-to-company-name/): Turn a list of domains into company names for free: read the name a site publishes about itself (schema.org Organization, og:site_name, title) with a tested Python script, and why WHOIS rarely helps.
- [How to check SPF and DMARC records (command line)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/check-spf-dmarc-record/): Check a domain's SPF and DMARC records from the command line with dig or nslookup, read what each part means, and count SPF DNS lookups against the limit of 10 with a tested Python script.
- [How to export Bluesky posts to CSV (any public profile)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/export-bluesky-posts/): Download all posts of any public Bluesky profile as CSV with the free public API (no account, no app password): a tested Python script with likes, reposts, replies and links, reply threads, and a full account backup.
- [How to get Steam reviews as JSON (appreviews API)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/steam-reviews-api/): Download Steam user reviews for any game with Steam's public appreviews endpoint: no API key, cursor paging, language and filter options, review score totals, and the fields you get (playtime, votes, thumbs up/down).
- [How to verify an email list (free checks first)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/verify-email-list-free/): Clean an email list before you send: what free checks catch (bad syntax, dead domains, null MX, disposable and role addresses, typos like gmial.com), a shell script for MX checks, and why mailbox (SMTP) checks are unreliable.
- [How to find out what technology a website uses](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/find-out-what-technology-a-website-uses/): Find out which CMS, JavaScript framework, hosting, CDN and analytics a website uses: read the HTTP headers and page source yourself, use a detector extension or lookup site, or check a whole list of sites at once.
- [How to check when an SSL certificate expires](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/check-ssl-certificate-expiry/): Find the expiry date of any site's SSL/TLS certificate in the browser or with openssl and curl, script a days-left check for a list of domains, and tell certificate expiry apart from domain (registration) expiry.
- [How to get App Store reviews as JSON (API and export)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/app-store-reviews-api/): Get Apple App Store reviews for any iPhone app as JSON with Apple's public customer-reviews feed: URL format, fields, paging, the 500-review limit per country, finding the app ID, and the App Store Connect API for your own apps.
- [How to get job postings from Greenhouse, Lever and Workday](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/greenhouse-lever-workday-jobs-api/): Pull a company's open jobs as JSON from its applicant tracking system: the public Greenhouse Job Board API, the Lever Postings API, and the endpoint Workday career sites use. Working curl examples, fields and limits.
- [How to extract all links from a web page](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/extract-all-links-from-web-page/): Get every URL on a web page as a list, CSV or Excel file: a one-line DevTools console snippet, a link-extractor extension, an online HTML link extractor, Python with BeautifulSoup, or a full-site crawl.
- [How to convert a web page to Markdown (for notes and LLMs)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/convert-web-page-to-markdown/): Save any article or web page as clean Markdown for Obsidian, notes or LLM prompts: a one-click browser extension, an in-browser HTML to Markdown converter, the trafilatura command line, or a hosted tool for many URLs.
- [How to modify HTTP request and response headers in Chrome and Firefox](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/modify-http-headers-in-chrome/): Change request headers (Authorization, User-Agent, Origin) and response headers (CORS, CSP) in your browser: Chrome DevTools overrides, Firefox Edit and Resend, curl, and header-editor extensions. What each one can and cannot do.
- [How to change the Referer, User-Agent or X-Forwarded-For header in Chrome](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/change-referer-user-agent-x-forwarded-for-chrome/): Set or remove the Referer, User-Agent, X-Forwarded-For, Origin and Authorization request headers in Chrome, and what the server still sees: navigator.userAgent, Sec-CH-UA client hints and your real IP.
- [How to hide or remove the Server header in nginx and Apache](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/remove-server-header-nginx-apache/): Stop nginx and Apache from sending their version number in the Server response header: server_tokens off, ServerTokens Prod, why 'Header unset Server' does nothing in Apache, and how to check the result with curl.
- [How to allow multiple origins in Access-Control-Allow-Origin (CORS)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/cors-allow-multiple-origins/): Access-Control-Allow-Origin takes one origin, not a list. Echo the request's Origin from an allow-list instead: a tested nginx map config, preflight handling, Vary: Origin, and the mistakes browsers reject.
- [How to get the color palette of any website](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/get-color-palette-from-website/): Extract a website's colors as hex codes, sorted by how often they're used, with a short DevTools console snippet, plus a second snippet that lists the site's CSS color variables (design tokens). Tested on Wikipedia, GitHub and Stripe.
- [How to export an HTML table to Excel with JavaScript](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/export-html-table-to-excel-javascript/): Add an 'Export to Excel' button to your page: a dependency-free CSV download (UTF-8 BOM, quoting, formula guard) and a real .xlsx with SheetJS table_to_book, including the raw option that keeps leading zeros.
- [Bearer token Authorization header: format and examples](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/bearer-token-authorization-header/): The exact format of the Authorization: Bearer header, with tested examples for curl, Python (requests and urllib) and JavaScript fetch, and what each one does with your token when the server redirects to another host.
- [X-Forwarded-For in nginx: log the real client IP without trusting forged headers](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/x-forwarded-for-real-ip-nginx/): Behind a reverse proxy or load balancer, nginx logs the proxy's IP. Use set_real_ip_from and real_ip_header to get the visitor's IP, and see the config that lets anyone forge their IP with one header.
- [HTTP header size limits: nginx 400 and Node 431 errors, measured](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/http-header-size-limit/): How big can request headers be? Measured limits for nginx (about 8 KB per header line by default) and Node.js (16 KB in total), the errors you get (400 Request Header Or Cookie Too Large, 431) and the settings that raise them.
- [400 Bad Request: Request Header Or Cookie Too Large (nginx), fixed and tested](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/request-header-or-cookie-too-large/): Why nginx answers 400 Request Header Or Cookie Too Large, measured: an 8 KB limit per header line (the whole Cookie line counts), 32 KB in total. How to fix it in Chrome by clearing one site's cookies, and on the server with large_client_header_buffers.
- [Sec-Fetch-Site, Sec-Fetch-Mode, Sec-Fetch-Dest and Sec-Fetch-User explained (tested in Chromium)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sec-fetch-site-mode-dest-headers/): What Chrome actually sends in Sec-Fetch-Site (none, same-origin, same-site, cross-site), Sec-Fetch-Mode (navigate, cors, no-cors), Sec-Fetch-Dest and Sec-Fetch-User for links, fetch, img, script, iframe, forms and window.open, plus a tested resource isolation policy.

- [Next.js global-error vs error for layout (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/nextjs-global-error-not-catching-layout/): We threw an error in Next.js app/layout.tsx and proved error.tsx never fires; only global-error.tsx catches it. Full HTTP responses and server logs included.
- [npm error code ENOENT (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/npm-error-code-enoent/): We reproduced npm's exact ENOENT error, plus 3 lookalikes (Missing script, MODULE_NOT_FOUND, EUSAGE) it's often confused with.
- [ESLint 'process'/'require'/'module' is not defined (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/eslint-process-require-module-is-not-defined/): We reproduced ESLint's 'process'/'require'/'module' is not defined no-undef errors on v9 and measured the exact flat-config and .eslintrc fixes.
- [git: unable to unlink / path is unmerged / object file is empty (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/git-unable-to-unlink-path-is-unmerged-object-file-is-empty/): We reproduced 3 distinct git errors — unable to unlink, path is unmerged, and object file is empty — and measured the exact fix for each.
- [postgres: must be owner of / permission denied for schema (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/postgres-must-be-owner-permission-denied-for-schema/): We reproduced Postgres's 'must be owner of table' and 'permission denied for schema' errors with two roles and measured the exact GRANT/ALTER fix for each.
- [yaml.scanner.ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/yaml-mapping-values-are-not-allowed-here/): We reproduced PyYAML's 'mapping values are not allowed here' error 2 ways and measured the exact fix: it's almost always an unquoted colon.
- [Hamilton: Required input missing / Cannot define function twice (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/apache-hamilton-required-input-missing-cannot-define-function/): We reproduced 3 real Hamilton dataflow errors — missing input, duplicate function, and a cyclic dependency — and measured the exact fix for each.
- [Terraform: Error acquiring the state lock (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/terraform-error-acquiring-the-state-lock/): We reproduced Terraform's state lock error with real concurrent runs and found force-unlock fails on a local backend — the lock had already released.
- [Terraform: Saved plan is stale (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/terraform-saved-plan-is-stale/): We reproduced Terraform's 'Saved plan is stale' error by applying an out-of-date plan file and measured the exact fix: regenerate the plan.
- [Terraform: Error: Cycle (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/terraform-error-cycle/): We made two Terraform resources reference each other and reproduced 'Error: Cycle', then measured the fix and that validate catches it too.
- [Terraform: Backend configuration changed (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/terraform-backend-configuration-changed/): We changed a Terraform backend path and measured the fix: -reconfigure alone still prompts; -migrate-state -force-copy is the non-interactive way to keep state.
- [Pytest: error: unrecognized arguments (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pytest-error-unrecognized-arguments/): We reproduced pytest's 'unrecognized arguments' error and measured that a missing plugin and a typo'd flag give the identical message and exit code 4.
- [Unittest discovery ImportError / _FailedTest (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/unittest-discovery-importerror-failedtest/): We broke a test file's import and measured that unittest discover hides the real traceback inside a fake _FailedTest case instead of showing it directly.
- [Pytest: no tests ran, exit code 5 (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pytest-no-tests-ran-exit-code-5/): We reproduced pytest exiting 5 with 'no tests ran' from a naming mismatch, a bad -k filter, and an empty directory, and measured the exact fix for each cause.
- [SQLite: database is locked (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-database-is-locked/): We reproduced Python sqlite3's 'database is locked' with a real concurrent write and measured the default 5s wait plus the timeout= fix that makes it succeed.
- [SQLite: attempt to write a readonly database (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-attempt-to-write-a-readonly-database/): We reproduced sqlite3's readonly-database error two ways: a read-only file, and a read-only directory with a writable file — both give the identical message.
- [SQLite: no such table (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-no-such-table/): We reproduced sqlite3's 'no such table' three ways and measured that table names are case-insensitive, so a casing mismatch is never the cause.
- [SQLite: database disk image is malformed (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-database-disk-image-is-malformed/): We corrupted a real SQLite file by truncation and measured exactly what triggers 'disk image is malformed': a page-count mismatch in the file header.
- [SQLite: unable to open database file (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-unable-to-open-database-file/): We reproduced sqlite3's 'unable to open database file' two ways: a missing parent directory, and a read-only directory for a brand-new file.
- [SQLite: table has no column named (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-has-no-column-named/): We reproduced sqlite3's 'has no column named' two ways: a typo'd column and an extra column, and measured that both give the identical error shape.
- [SQLite: no such column (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-no-such-column/): We reproduced sqlite3's 'no such column' from a SELECT list, a WHERE clause, and ORDER BY, plus the distinct ambiguous-column error from a JOIN.
- [SQLite: cannot start a transaction within a transaction (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-cannot-start-a-transaction-within-a-transaction/): We reproduced sqlite3's transaction-nesting error, including the sneaky case: Python opens a transaction implicitly before your explicit BEGIN ever runs.
- [SQLite: cannot commit - no transaction is active (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-cannot-commit-no-transaction-is-active/): We measured a real split in sqlite3: con.commit() silently no-ops with nothing open, but the raw SQL COMMIT statement raises an error for the exact same state.
- [SQLite: NOT NULL constraint failed (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-not-null-constraint-failed/): We reproduced sqlite3's NOT NULL error from an explicit NULL and from simply omitting the column, and measured that a column DEFAULT fixes both identically.
- [SQLite: datatype mismatch (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-datatype-mismatch/): We measured why SQLite accepts text in an INTEGER column everywhere except one place: an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, where it raises 'datatype mismatch' instead.
- [SQLite: too many SQL variables (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-too-many-sql-variables/): We measured the real bound-parameter limit on a live system: 250,000, not the commonly-cited 999 or 32,766 — it's set at compile time and varies by distro.
- [SQLite: CHECK constraint failed (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-check-constraint-failed/): We reproduced sqlite3's CHECK constraint error and measured that the message echoes the exact expression, and that NULL silently bypasses CHECK entirely.
- [SQLite: UNIQUE constraint failed (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-unique-constraint-failed/): We reproduced sqlite3's UNIQUE error, measured that NULL is exempt (two NULLs insert fine), and confirmed the ON CONFLICT upsert fix.
- [SQLite: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-foreign-key-constraint-failed/): We measured that SQLite's foreign keys are OFF by default (a missing-parent insert succeeds silently) until PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is set per connection.
- [SQLite: Incomplete Input / Unrecognized Token (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/sqlite-incomplete-input/): We reproduced SQLite's three distinct syntax-error messages in Python: incomplete input, unrecognized token, and near X: syntax error.
- [TypeError: Object of type X Is Not JSON Serializable (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-object-not-json-serializable/): We measured why json.dumps() rejects datetime, set, bytes and Decimal, why int dict keys silently become strings, and the default= fix, in Python 3.13.
- [json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Extra Data (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-decode-error-extra-data/): We measured why json.loads() throws Extra Data on concatenated JSON and JSON Lines files, and the exact raw_decode() fix for both, in Python 3.13.
- [json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Invalid Control Character (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-decode-error-invalid-control-character/): We measured why a raw newline or tab inside a JSON string breaks json.loads(), why json.dumps() never does it, and the strict=False fix, in Python 3.13.
- [Expecting Property Name Enclosed in Double Quotes (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-expecting-property-name-double-quotes/): We measured the three causes of this JSONDecodeError: single-quoted keys, unquoted keys, and the classic str(dict) instead of json.dumps() mistake.
- [ValueError: Circular Reference Detected (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-circular-reference-detected/): We measured why json.dumps() raises this on self-referencing data, why default= can't fix it, and the recursive sanitizer that does, in Python 3.13.
- [TypeError: the JSON Object Must Be str, bytes or bytearray (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-object-must-be-str-bytes-bytearray/): We measured four causes of this TypeError: passing a file object, None, an already-parsed dict, or a custom object to json.loads() instead of json.load().
- [json.dumps() sort_keys=True TypeError (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-dumps-sort-keys-typeerror/): We measured why adding sort_keys=True can suddenly break json.dumps() on mixed-type dict keys, and which key-type mixes are actually safe.
- [TypeError: Object of Type int64 Is Not JSON Serializable (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-numpy-int64-not-json-serializable/): We measured why json.dumps() rejects numpy int64 and ndarray but not float64, and the fastest default= fix, with numpy 2.5 and pandas 3.0.
- [json.dumps() ensure_ascii Unicode Escapes (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-dumps-ensure-ascii-unicode-escapes/): We measured why json.dumps() escapes non-ASCII text to \uXXXX by default, that both forms decode the same, and the byte-size tradeoff of turning it off.
- [json.dumps() separators= Silently Produces Broken JSON (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-dumps-separators-silently-broken/): We measured that swapping json.dumps()'s separators= tuple order produces invalid JSON with zero error at dump time — it fails later, only when parsed.
- [json.dumps() indent= TypeError: can't multiply sequence by non-int (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/json-dumps-indent-typeerror-cant-multiply-sequence/): We measured json.dumps(indent=): floats raise a confusing TypeError, bool is silently accepted (bool is an int), negatives are clamped to zero with no error.
- [csv.Error: field larger than field limit (131072) (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-error-field-larger-than-field-limit/): We measured Python's csv field size limit: exactly 131072 characters (not bytes), global across every reader, and a negative limit silently breaks all parsing.
- [csv.Error: new-line character seen in unquoted field (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-error-new-line-character-seen-in-unquoted-field/): We measured csv's new-line error: an embedded raw newline outside quotes triggers it, and the error's own newline='' suggested fix often doesn't apply.
- [csv DictReader/DictWriter Ragged Rows: the None Key (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-dictreader-dictwriter-ragged-rows-none-key/): We measured csv on ragged rows: DictReader never raises (short rows get None, long rows nest under a literal None key) but DictWriter raises on an extra key.
- [csv.Error: need to escape, but no escapechar set (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-error-need-to-escape-but-no-escapechar-set/): We measured csv.writer's QUOTE_NONE: a field with the delimiter raises unless escapechar is set. Also: QUOTE_NONNUMERIC reading always returns float, never int.
- [csv.Sniffer() Silently Guesses a Wrong Delimiter (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-sniffer-wrong-delimiter-silently-guessed/): We measured csv.Sniffer() pick the letter 'm' as delimiter for plain prose, zero error — it favors the most consistent per-line count, not the sensible char.
- [csv.Sniffer().has_header() False Negative (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-sniffer-has-header-false-negative/): We measured csv.Sniffer().has_header() return False for a real header like 'fruit,color' — it only detects a header when column types differ from the body.
- [csv.reader Ignores lineterminator= (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-reader-ignores-lineterminator/): We measured csv.reader() ignoring lineterminator= entirely — only the writer uses it. Setting it on a reader doesn't error, it just fails to split rows.
- [csv.register_dialect() Overwrites 'excel' (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-register-dialect-silently-overwrites-excel/): We measured csv.register_dialect('excel', ...) silently replacing the built-in dialect process-wide — but only some csv callers actually pick up the change.
- [subprocess shell=True Drops List Args (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/subprocess-shell-true-list-args-silently-dropped/): We measured subprocess.run([...], shell=True) silently dropping every argument after the first — no error, exit code 0, just missing output.
- [Popen.communicate(timeout=) Leaves Process Running (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/subprocess-communicate-timeout-does-not-kill-process/): We measured Popen.communicate(timeout=1) raising TimeoutExpired while leaving the child process running — you have to kill it yourself.
- [subprocess env= Replaces, Doesn't Merge (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/subprocess-env-parameter-replaces-entire-environment/): We measured subprocess.run(..., env={...}) wiping out every inherited variable, including PATH and HOME, not just adding to them.
- [CalledProcessError.stderr Is None By Default (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/subprocess-calledprocesserror-stderr-is-none-by-default/): We measured catching CalledProcessError without capture_output= and finding e.stderr is None — the real error text went straight to the terminal instead.
- [zlib decompressobj max_length Silent Data Loss (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/zlib-decompressobj-max-length-unconsumed-tail-silent-data-loss/): We measured decompressobj().decompress(data, max_length) silently returning 270 bytes instead of 11000 when unconsumed_tail isn't fed back in.
- [zlib compressobj flush() Ends the Stream (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/zlib-compressobj-flush-default-ends-the-stream/): We measured compressobj().flush() with no argument, then compress() again, raising "inconsistent stream state" — default flush ends the stream for good.
- [zlib crc32 Per-Chunk Sums Are Wrong (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/zlib-crc32-chunk-checksums-cannot-be-added-together/): We measured adding two zlib.crc32() chunk checksums together producing a completely wrong value — the correct way is to chain the running value forward.
- [gzip Output Is Not Reproducible By Default (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/gzip-output-is-not-reproducible-by-default/): We measured gzip.compress() output differing on every run for the same input — a timestamp and filename land in the header, breaking hashes and build caches.
- [subprocess text=True Decode Error Loses returncode (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/subprocess-text-true-raises-unicodedecodeerror-loses-returncode/): We measured subprocess.run(text=True) raising UnicodeDecodeError on one bad byte — the exception has no returncode, pid, or success status at all.
- [subprocess shell=True kill() Leaves Child Running (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/subprocess-shell-true-kill-leaves-child-process-running/): We measured proc.kill() on a shell=True Popen only killing the /bin/sh wrapper — the actual command it ran kept running as an orphan process afterward.
- [csv DictWriter Forgetting writeheader() (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-dictwriter-forgetting-writeheader-corrupts-data-silently/): We measured csv.DictWriter skipping the header row silently when writeheader() isn't called — DictReader then treats your first real row as the header.
- [zlib decompress() Drops Concatenated Streams (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/zlib-decompress-silently-drops-concatenated-streams/): We measured zlib.decompress() on two concatenated zlib streams silently returning only the first one's data — the second stream is discarded with no error.
- [subprocess stdin.write() Deadlock Without communicate() (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/subprocess-stdin-write-deadlocks-without-communicate/): We measured writing 1MB to proc.stdin without reading stdout concurrently hanging forever — the child's full output pipe blocks it from reading more input.
- [csv QUOTE_NONNUMERIC Booleans Round-Trip Failure (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/csv-quote-nonnumeric-writes-booleans-unquoted-breaks-reading/): We measured csv.writer(quoting=QUOTE_NONNUMERIC) writing True/False unquoted since bool is a number subtype — reading that same file back then crashes.
- [configparser Percent Sign InterpolationSyntaxError (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/configparser-percent-sign-raises-interpolationsyntaxerror/): We measured configparser.ConfigParser() raising InterpolationSyntaxError on an ordinary value like '50% off' — the default interpolation treats % as special.
- [configparser getboolean() Rejects enabled/disabled (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/configparser-getboolean-rejects-enabled-disabled/): We measured ConfigParser.getboolean() accepting yes/no/true/false/on/off/1/0 (case-insensitive) but raising ValueError on the equally common enabled/disabled.
- [configparser ${} Syntax Silently Not Interpolated (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/configparser-dollar-brace-syntax-silently-not-interpolated/): We measured ConfigParser's default interpolation leaving ${section:option} unexpanded with no error, returning literal text. Fix: pass ExtendedInterpolation().
- [configparser read() Missing File No Error (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/configparser-read-missing-file-no-error/): We measured ConfigParser.read() returning an empty list on a missing file, no exception, leaving the parser silently empty instead of raising FileNotFoundError.
- [configparser remove_option() Silent No-op on DEFAULT Fallback (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/configparser-remove-option-silent-noop-on-default-fallback/): We measured remove_option() returning False and doing nothing on a [DEFAULT]-only key, even though has_option() and 'in' both say it's present.
- [argparse type=bool Always True Except Empty String (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/argparse-type-bool-always-true-except-empty-string/): We measured --flag type=bool parsing 'False', '0', and 'no' as True. Only an empty string parses False. Fix: action='store_true' or BooleanOptionalAction.
- [argparse Subparsers Not Required by Default (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/argparse-subparsers-not-required-by-default-attributeerror-later/): We measured parse_args([]) succeeding with no sub-command chosen, silently omitting every sub-command-only argument instead of erroring at parse time.
- [argparse Negative Number Positional Breaks With a -1-style Option (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/argparse-negative-number-positional-breaks-if-any-option-looks-like-one/): We measured a working 'value -5' positional failing with 'unrecognized arguments: -5' as soon as the parser gained any -1-style option. Fix: a -- separator.
- [urlencode() List Value Without doseq Encodes str(list) (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/urlencode-list-value-without-doseq-encodes-str-of-list/): We measured urlencode({'a': [1,2,3]}) producing a=%5B1%2C+2%2C+3%5D instead of three repeated a= pairs, with no error. Fix: doseq=True.
- [urljoin() //host Input Silently Switches Host (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/urljoin-double-slash-input-silently-switches-host/): We measured urljoin(base, '//evil.example.com/x') returning a URL on evil.example.com, not the base's host, with no error. Risky if the 2nd arg is user input.
- [argparse default Not Validated Against choices (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/argparse-default-not-validated-against-choices/): We measured a default not in choices= passing through silently when the flag is omitted, but rejected the moment a user types that exact value explicitly.
- [urllib.parse.quote() Double-Encoding Corrupts Already-Encoded Values (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/quote-double-encoding-silently-corrupts-already-encoded-values/): We measured quote() on an already-encoded string re-encoding the % sign itself, so caf%C3%A9 becomes caf%25C3%25A9 and decodes back wrong, no error.
- [parse_qsl() Drops Empty Values By Default (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/parse-qsl-drops-empty-values-by-default/): We measured parse_qsl('a=1&b=&c=3') silently omitting b entirely instead of returning ('b', ''). Fix: keep_blank_values=True.
- [urlparse() Without a Scheme Misreads the Host (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/urlparse-without-scheme-misreads-host-as-path-or-scheme/): We measured urlparse('example.com/path') putting it all in .path (.hostname None), and 'example.com:8080/path' reading 'example.com' as scheme, not host.
- [tarfile.extractall() Path Traversal Still Not Blocked By Default (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/tarfile-extractall-path-traversal-not-blocked-by-default/): We measured extractall() writing a '../outside.txt' member outside the dest dir on Python 3.13, no exception -- just a warning. filter='data' blocks it.
- [datetime.astimezone() on a Naive Value Silently Assumes Local Time (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/datetime-astimezone-on-naive-datetime-silently-assumes-local-tz/): We measured .astimezone() on a naive UTC value returning a time off by the full UTC offset, no exception -- fixed with .replace(tzinfo=utc) first.
- [Two Different DST Fall-Back Instants Compare Equal in datetime (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/datetime-dst-fallback-ambiguous-time-compares-equal-to-different-instant/): We measured two zoneinfo-aware datetimes an hour apart in real UTC time (DST fall-back ambiguity) returning == True, equal hash(), and a 0:00:00 subtraction.
- [shutil.copytree() Leaves a Partial Copy Behind When It Raises (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/shutil-copytree-leaves-partial-copy-behind-when-it-raises/): We measured copytree() raising shutil.Error on one unreadable file but still leaving every other file it already copied sitting in the destination directory.
- [shutil.make_archive() Stores Symlinks as Absolute Paths in tar Format (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/shutil-make-archive-tar-stores-symlinks-as-absolute-paths/): We measured make_archive() storing a symlink's absolute target in tar format while zip just followed it -- and filter='data' then refuses to extract that tar.
- [isinstance(x, date) Silently Matches datetime Too (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/datetime-isinstance-date-check-silently-matches-datetime-too/): We measured isinstance(datetime.now(), date) returning True, so a dispatch function checking date before datetime silently misroutes every datetime value.
- [tarfile.open() Write Mode Ignores the .tar.gz Extension (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/tarfile-open-write-mode-w-does-not-auto-compress-by-extension/): We measured tarfile.open('x.tar.gz', 'w') writing a plain tar despite the .gz name -- gzip.open() and system tar both reject the file as not gzipped.
- [timedelta.days Is -1 for Any Negative Sub-Day Duration (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/timedelta-days-attribute-is-negative-one-for-any-negative-sub-day-duration/): We measured timedelta(hours=-1).days returning -1, not 0 -- any negative duration under a full day still reports .days as -1, which breaks naive age-check code.
- [pathlib Path.exists() Returns False for a Dangling Symlink (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pathlib-exists-returns-false-for-a-dangling-symlink/): We measured Path.exists() returning False for a symlink whose target is missing, even though is_symlink() is True and the entry still shows up in os.listdir().
- [pathlib glob() Matches Hidden Dotfiles, glob Module Does Not (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pathlib-glob-matches-hidden-dotfiles-unlike-glob-module/): We measured Path.glob('*.txt') matching a hidden .txt file that glob.glob('*.txt') skips -- pathlib has no dotfile-skipping rule, unlike the glob module.
- [pathlib Path.resolve() Does Not Detect a Symlink Loop by Default (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pathlib-resolve-does-not-detect-a-symlink-loop-by-default/): We measured Path.resolve() default strict=False returning a symlink-loop path unchanged instead of raising -- the failure surfaces later when it's opened.
- [pathlib Path.walk() Puts Symlinked Directories in files, Not dirs (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pathlib-path-walk-puts-symlinked-directories-in-files-not-dirs/): We measured Path.walk() putting a symlinked directory in the files list, not dirs -- the opposite of os.walk(), which puts the same symlink in dirs by default.
- [fnmatch Asterisk Matches Across Path Separators, Unlike glob (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/fnmatch-asterisk-matches-across-path-separators-unlike-glob/): We measured fnmatch.fnmatch('temp/*.txt', ...) matching files deep under temp/ -- its * has no rule against matching a slash, unlike glob.
- [difflib quick_ratio() Returns 1.0 for Completely Reordered Strings (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/difflib-quick-ratio-returns-1-for-completely-reordered-strings/): We measured SequenceMatcher.quick_ratio() returning 1.0 for 'abcdefgh' vs its reverse, while the real ratio() is 0.125 -- quick_ratio ignores order entirely.
- [difflib unified_diff() Glues Lines Together Without Trailing Newlines (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/difflib-unified-diff-glues-lines-together-without-trailing-newlines/): We measured unified_diff() output becoming one garbled line when input came from split('\n') instead of splitlines(keepends=True) -- silently, no error.
- [glob.glob() Silently Fails to Find a Filename Containing Brackets (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/glob-glob-silently-fails-to-find-a-filename-containing-brackets/): We measured glob.glob() given the literal filename 'file[1].txt' returning 'file1.txt' instead -- [1] is parsed as a character class, not literal brackets.
- [glob.glob(recursive=True) Does Not Detect a Symlink Loop (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/glob-recursive-true-does-not-detect-a-symlink-loop/): We measured glob.glob('**', recursive=True) walking ~40 levels into a symlink loop before ELOOP stopped it, returning 83 nested paths instead of stopping there.
- [fnmatch Bracket Caret Is Literal, Not Negation (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/fnmatch-bracket-caret-is-literal-not-negation/): We measured fnmatch treating [^t] as a literal char class, not negation -- it matched files the regex-style pattern meant to exclude. Use [!t] instead.
- [glob.glob() Over-Matches Filenames Containing * or ? (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/glob-glob-over-matches-filenames-containing-asterisk-or-question-mark/): We measured glob.glob() on a file named 'data*.csv' silently pulling in 2 unrelated files -- the '*' expands as wildcard, not literal. Fix: glob.escape().

- [textwrap.dedent() Does Nothing on Mixed Tabs/Spaces (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/textwrap-dedent-does-nothing-on-mixed-tabs-and-spaces/): We measured textwrap.dedent() leaving text unchanged when lines mix tab and space indentation -- no common prefix exists, so nothing is stripped, no error.
- [textwrap.shorten() Drops a Too-Long Word Entirely (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/textwrap-shorten-drops-a-too-long-word-entirely/): We measured textwrap.shorten() returning only '[...]' with no original text when one word exceeds the width -- unlike wrap(), it never partially breaks it.
- [textwrap Splits Hyphenated CLI Flags Mid-Name by Default (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/textwrap-splits-hyphenated-cli-flags-mid-name/): We measured textwrap splitting '--enable-verbose-logging' at an internal hyphen -- argparse's own --help output hits this bug. Fix: break_on_hyphens=False.
- [itertools.groupby Groups Go Empty If Not Read Right Away (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/itertools-groupby-groups-go-empty-if-not-read-right-away/): We measured itertools.groupby in Python 3.13.5: collecting (key, group) pairs first, reading later, returns empty lists, no error -- groups share one iterator.

- [itertools.islice Start/Stop Are Relative, Not Fixed Indices (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/itertools-islice-start-stop-are-relative-not-fixed-indices/): We measured itertools.islice in Python 3.13.5: calling islice(it, 2, 5) twice on one iterator with identical args returns two different slices.

- [itertools.starmap() vs map(): The Confusing Missing-Argument Error (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/itertools-starmap-vs-map-confusing-missing-argument-error/): We measured passing a list of tuples to map() in Python 3.13.5: it fails with a missing-argument TypeError that never mentions tuples. starmap() is the fix.

Same n, three different lengths.

- [bisect: key= Only Transforms the List, Never the Search Value (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-bisect-key-only-transforms-the-list-not-the-search-value/): We measured Python 3.13.5: bisect_left(a, x, key=f) applies f() to every element of a, never to x -- the wrong form of x errors, or gives a wrong index.
- [bisect: hi < lo Silently Corrupts insort's Sort Order (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-bisect-insort-hi-less-than-lo-silently-corrupts-sort-order/): We measured Python 3.13.5: bisect validates a negative lo but never checks hi < lo -- insort_right can insert into the middle of a sorted list with zero error.
- [struct: unpack_from() Silently Ignores Trailing Bytes unpack() Rejects (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-struct-unpack-from-silently-ignores-trailing-bytes/): We measured Python 3.13.5: struct.unpack() errors on extra trailing bytes, but unpack_from() silently ignores anything past what it needs on the same data.
- [contextlib: closing() Masks the Real Error If close() Is Missing (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-contextlib-closing-masks-real-error-if-close-missing/): We measured Python 3.13.5: contextlib.closing() checks for close() only at exit -- if missing, AttributeError buries the real exception raised inside the block.
- [contextlib: ExitStack Silently Drops All But One Callback Error (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-contextlib-exitstack-drops-all-but-one-callback-error/): We measured Python 3.13.5: when multiple ExitStack callbacks raise, only the last-executed one propagates -- the rest vanish, not even chained as __context__.
- [contextlib: redirect_stdout() Redirects Every Thread, Not Just Yours (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-contextlib-redirect-stdout-affects-every-thread/): We measured Python 3.13.5: redirect_stdout() reassigns the global sys.stdout -- a concurrent threads print() calls get silently captured into your buffer too.
- [contextlib: suppress(GeneratorExit) Breaks Generator close() (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-contextlib-suppress-generatorexit-breaks-close/): We measured Python 3.13.5: suppressing GeneratorExit then reaching another yield makes a generators close() raise RuntimeError instead of closing cleanly.
- [heapq: A Single NaN Silently Corrupts the Whole Heap Invariant (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-heapq-nan-silently-corrupts-heap-invariant/): We measured Python 3.13.5: heapify()/heappush() with one NaN gives no error, but heappop() can return even the non-NaN values out of order.
- [shelve: Without writeback=True, a Mutation Vanishes in the Same Session (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-shelve-writeback-false-mutation-lost-same-session/): We measured Python 3.13.5: shelve without writeback=True returns a fresh object every read, so in-place mutations vanish instantly, same session.
- [weakref: WeakValueDictionary Iteration Silently Skips GC'd Entries (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-weakref-weakvaluedictionary-iteration-silently-skips-entries/): We measured Python 3.13.5: dropping the last strong ref during iteration silently removes it from a WeakValueDictionary, no RuntimeError, unlike a plain dict.
- [weakref.finalize(obj, obj.method) Silently Keeps obj Alive Forever (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-weakref-finalize-bound-method-keeps-object-alive/): We measured Python 3.13.5: passing a bound method as the finalize callback keeps a strong ref, so the object is never collected and cleanup never runs early.
- [calendar.itermonthdates() Crashes on December 9999 -- Sibling Methods Don't (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-calendar-itermonthdates-crashes-year-9999-december/): We measured Python 3.13.5: itermonthdates(9999,12) raises ValueError, while itermonthdays2/3/4 return the identical month grid fine -- same data, no crash.
- [functools.lru_cache Confuses 1 and True in Some Calls, Not Others (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-lru-cache-int-bool-cache-collision/): We measured Python 3.13.5: lru_cache(g)(1,0) then g(True,False) returns the cached int result, not a fresh bool one -- same hash, same ==, no error.
- [functools.partial Objects With Identical Args Are Never Equal (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-partial-never-equal-breaks-dedup/): We measured Python 3.13.5: two functools.partial(f,1,2) objects, same func and args, are not ==, hash differently, and both land in a set meant to dedupe them.
- [functools.lru_cache Treats Keyword Argument Order as Part of the Cache Key (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-lru-cache-kwarg-order-cache-miss/): We measured Python 3.13.5: f(a=1,b=2) and f(b=2,a=1) are the same call, but lru_cache caches them as two separate entries -- kwarg order changes the cache key.
- [functools.cached_property Writes to a Frozen Dataclass's __dict__ Anyway (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-cached-property-mutates-frozen-dataclass/): We measured Python 3.13.5: Point(3,4) is frozen -- p.x=10 raises FrozenInstanceError -- but p.magnitude (a cached_property) writes to p.__dict__ with no error.
- [functools.partialmethod Binds One Shared Mutable Object to Every Instance (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-partialmethod-shares-mutable-keyword-argument/): We measured Python 3.13.5: partialmethod(configure, options={}) binds the same dict to every instance and call -- mutating it in one leaks into all others.
- [functools.singledispatchmethod Register on a Subclass Leaks Into the Base Class (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-singledispatchmethod-subclass-register-leaks-to-base/): We measured Python 3.13.5: registering on a subclass's inherited singledispatchmethod changes the base class's dispatch too -- one shared registry.
- [functools.cached_property Lost Its Thread-Safety Lock in Python 3.12 (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-cached-property-thread-race-3-12/): We measured Python 3.13.5: 10 threads hitting one cached_property at once ran the getter 10 times, not once -- the pre-3.12 per-instance lock is gone.
- [functools.wraps on a functools.partial Copies the Wrong __doc__/__module__ (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-functools-wraps-partial-wrong-metadata/): We measured Python 3.13.5: wraps() on a functools.partial object silently sets __doc__/__module__ to generic partial-class values, not the wrapped call's own.
- [copy.deepcopy Copies a functools.cached_property's Stale Cached Value (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-copy-deepcopy-cached-property-stale-value/): We measured Python 3.13.5: deepcopy copies a cached_property's stored value as plain data -- it never recomputes, even after the source attribute changed.
- [inspect.getmembers Silently Skips AttributeError but Crashes on Any Other Exception (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-inspect-getmembers-property-exception-crashes-everything/): We measured Python 3.13.5: a property raising AttributeError is silently skipped by getmembers(), but ValueError (or any other exception) aborts the whole call.
- [collections.abc .register() Makes isinstance Pass But Grants No Methods (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-collections-abc-register-isinstance-lies-no-mixins/): We measured Python 3.13.5: Mapping.register(Cls) makes isinstance(obj, Mapping) True, but obj.get()/.keys() still don't exist -- no code is granted.
- [collections.abc.Sequence __iter__/in Loop Forever Without IndexError (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-collections-abc-sequence-iter-contains-infinite-loop/): We measured Python 3.13.5: Sequence's mixin __iter__/__contains__ call __getitem__(0,1,...) until IndexError. Return None instead, both loop forever.
- [collections.abc.Set operators raise TypeError without _from_iterable override (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-collections-abc-set-operators-from-iterable-typeerror/): We measured Python 3.13.5: Set's &, |, -, ^ build results via cls(iterable) -- an __init__ needing a 2nd arg makes all of them raise TypeError.
- [collections.abc.Hashable isinstance() Cache Goes Stale (Tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-collections-abc-hashable-isinstance-stale-cache/): We measured Python 3.13.5: isinstance(x, Hashable) keeps returning True after __hash__ is set to None on the class, even though hash(x) now raises TypeError.

- [io.TextIOWrapper Crashes on a Non-Blocking Raw Stream's None (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-io-textiowrapper-none-readinto-typeerror/): We measured Python 3.13.5: a non-blocking raw stream's None read result works fine via BufferedReader, but TextIOWrapper.read() on it raises TypeError.
- [io.TextIOWrapper.detach() Leaves the Raw Stream Past Your Last Read (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-io-textiowrapper-detach-raw-stream-position-mismatch/): We measured Python 3.13.5: reading 5 chars via TextIOWrapper then detach() leaves the raw stream at byte 54 of 54, not byte 5 -- read-ahead, not text position.

Mid-Write Silently Drops Characters (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-io-textiowrapper-reconfigure-errors-mid-write/): We measured Python 3.13.5: reconfigure(errors=...) is unrestricted on the write side -- switching to errors=ignore mid-stream silently drops characters.

Text-mode files raise TypeError; json= is dropped.

- [SciPy and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/scipy-numpy-2-compatibility/): Old SciPy on NumPy 2 fails with multiarray failed to import, numpy.dtype size changed, or cannot import Inf. SciPy 1.13+ supports NumPy 2. Tested fixes.
- [Matplotlib and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/matplotlib-numpy-2-compatibility/): import matplotlib fails on NumPy 2 with numpy.core.multiarray failed to import on 3.8.3 and older. Matplotlib 3.8.4 is the first that works. Tested fixes.
- [ImportError: Numba needs NumPy 2.2 or less (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/numba-needs-numpy-2-2-or-less/): import numba fails with "Numba needs NumPy 2.2 or less" (or 2.0 or less). Which NumPy each Numba release allows, and two tested fixes.
- [PyArrow and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pyarrow-numpy-2-compatibility/): import pyarrow fails on NumPy 2 with _ARRAY_API not found and numpy.core.multiarray failed to import. PyArrow 16.0.0 is the first that works. Tested fixes.
- [statsmodels and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/statsmodels-numpy-2-compatibility/): statsmodels 0.14.1 fails on NumPy 2 with numpy.dtype size changed; 0.14.2 is the first that works. Plus the scipy _lazywhere and pandas 3 errors. Tested.
- [gensim: cannot import name 'triu' from 'scipy.linalg' (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/gensim-cannot-import-name-triu-from-scipy-linalg/): import gensim fails: cannot import name 'triu' from 'scipy.linalg' on SciPy 1.13+. Upgrade to gensim 4.4.0 or pin scipy<1.13. Plus the NumPy 2 error, tested.
- [shap and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/shap-numpy-2-compatibility/): shap 0.45 and older print C extension was not built during install! and fail with numpy.core.multiarray failed to import on NumPy 2. 0.46.0 works. Tested.
- [spaCy and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/spacy-numpy-2-compatibility/): import spacy fails with numpy.dtype size changed in thinc numpy_ops after NumPy 2 is installed. spaCy 3.8 with thinc 8.3 works. Tested fixes.
- [PyTables and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/pytables-numpy-2-compatibility/): import tables fails on NumPy 2 with numpy.dtype size changed in utilsextension. PyTables 3.10.1 is the first that works; 3.9.2 is uncapped. Tested fixes.
- [astropy and NumPy 2 compatibility (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/astropy-numpy-2-compatibility/): astropy 6.0 fails on NumPy 2 (numpy.dtype size changed); 6.1 to 7.1 fail on NumPy 2.4 (no attribute 'in1d'). 7.2.0 works. Tested fixes.
- [NumPy 2.4: module 'numpy' has no attribute 'in1d' / 'trapz' (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/numpy-has-no-attribute-in1d-trapz/): NumPy 2.4 removed np.in1d and np.trapz. Use np.isin and np.trapezoid. NumPy 2.3 vs 2.4 output, tested, plus what to do when a library calls them.
- [scikit-learn-extra + NumPy 2: dtype size changed (tested fixes)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/scikit-learn-extra-numpy-2/): scikit-learn-extra 0.3.0 fails to import on NumPy 2 (dtype size changed in _cyfht). Tested fixes: numpy<2, install from GitHub main, or the kmedoids package.
- [librosa + NumPy 2: works; the real error is pkg_resources (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/librosa-numpy-2-compatibility/): librosa 0.10.2+ runs on NumPy 2.4 (tested). Older librosa fails with No module named 'pkg_resources' (setuptools 82+), not NumPy. Fixes, tested.
- [TensorBoard: No module named 'pkg_resources' (tested fix)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/no-module-named-pkg-resources-tensorboard/): tensorboard 2.20 and older import pkg_resources, which setuptools 82 removed. Tested fixes: upgrade to tensorboard 2.21.0 or pin setuptools<81.
- [cx_Oracle install: No module named 'pkg_resources' (tested fix)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/no-module-named-pkg-resources-cx-oracle/): pip install cx_Oracle fails with No module named 'pkg_resources', even with setuptools. Tested fixes: oracledb, --build-constraint, no build isolation.
- [selenium-wire: No module named 'pkg_resources' / blinker._saferef (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/no-module-named-pkg-resources-selenium-wire/): from seleniumwire import webdriver fails with No module named 'pkg_resources', then blinker._saferef. Tested fix: pin setuptools<81 and blinker<1.8.
- [openai CLIP: No module named 'pkg_resources' on pip install (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/no-module-named-pkg-resources-clip/): pip install git+https://github.com/openai/CLIP.git fails with No module named 'pkg_resources'. Fix: install main or --build-constraint setuptools<81.
- [uv: No module named 'pkg_resources' when building a package (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/no-module-named-pkg-resources-uv/): uv add fails building an sdist with No module named 'pkg_resources'. The hint's fix fails; build-constraint-dependencies setuptools<81 works.
- [Poetry: No module named 'pkg_resources' (PEP517 build failed, tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/no-module-named-pkg-resources-poetry/): poetry add fails with PEP517 build of a dependency failed: No module named 'pkg_resources'. Tested fix: [tool.poetry.build-constraints] setuptools<81.
- [pipenv: No module named 'pkg_resources' (hidden lock error, tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/no-module-named-pkg-resources-pipenv/): pipenv install fails with 'dependencies could not be resolved' but the cause is a hidden No module named 'pkg_resources'. Tested fix: PIP_BUILD_CONSTRAINT.

Tested Dockerfile fix for pip 24 and 26: PIP_CONSTRAINT + PIP_BUILD_CONSTRAINT.

What it means (setuptools 82 removes it), how to find the importer, and two tested ways to silence it.

- [Content-Type charset=utf-8 (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/content-type-charset-utf-8/): We served the same UTF-8 text under 13 Content-Type and meta variants in Chromium 153. Without a charset it rendered cafÃ© as windows-1252; the header beat meta, a BOM beat the header, fetch().text() ignored it. Plus Python requests, Node, Express and nginx fixes.
- [Location header: relative vs absolute URLs (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/location-header-relative-vs-absolute/): Relative Location values like next, /next, ../x, //host/x and ?q=1 resolved the same in Chromium 153, curl 8.14.1 and Node 24 fetch on every 3xx code. Plus: POST becoming GET on 301/302/303, Location on 201 is never followed, and why fetch redirect: manual hides it.
- [TypeError: object is not subscriptable (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-typeerror-object-is-not-subscriptable/): We reproduced TypeError: object is not subscriptable on Python 3.13.5: list.sort() returning None, int, float, custom classes, and functions. Exact fixes.
- [re.error: nothing to repeat (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/python-re-error-nothing-to-repeat/): We triggered Python's regex 'nothing to repeat' and 'multiple repeat' errors 5 ways and measured the exact position and fix for each.
- [Vite dependency-optimization crash (tested)](https://honestkit.github.io/guides/vite-dependency-optimization-crash/): We crashed Vite 8.3.2's dev server with one broken dependency and measured the exact fix (optimizeDeps.exclude) that keeps it running.
